rows.author: K077;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING AN AMBER ALERT SYSTEM TO PREVENT KIDNAPPING OF CHILDREN
rows.abstract:
Defines AMBER (Abducted and Missing Child Broadcast Emergency Response) Alert System as a system that alerts the public regarding a missing child. Seeks to provide a rapid response mechanism designed to quickly disseminate information about the disappearance of a child who is at risk of death or serious injury. 

Proposes that the Department of Interior and Local Government (DILG) shall establish the Alert System in coordination with the Department of Justice (DOJ) and other relevant enforcement agencies, broadcast media entities, and social media platforms.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2024-04-29

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING AND STRENGTHENING THE FOOD STAMP PROGRAM OF THE DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL WELFARE AND DEVELOPMENT, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF
rows.abstract:
Seeks to provide food assistance among eligible individuals and families belonging to the marginalized or disadvantaged sectors of society. 

Intends to reduce hunger and improve nutrition through a monthly meal augmentation valued at P3,000.00. Provides mechanisms for targeting beneficiaries and improving program accessibility to alleviate poverty and food insecurity.

rows.author: K122;
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A PROPERTY REGIME FOR COHABITING SAME SEX PARTNERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Proposes to establish legal frameworks governing property rights and obligations for LGBTQ+ (lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer) or same-sex couples. Seeks to ensure equity and fairness in property division; defines property rights; outlines procedures for joint ownership; and addresses the dissolution of the partnership. 

Includes other provisions such as donations and gifts received by any of the parties during the cohabitation and personal debts, loans, and other financial obligations or liabilities incurred by any of the partners.
Â
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2024-04-29

rows.author: F028;
rows.title_full: "AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE PHILIPPINE CROP INSURANCE CORPORATION (PCIC) BY INTRODUCING A MARKET-BASED REFORM ON AGRICULTURAL INSURANCE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSE"
rows.abstract:
Defines several terms such as Agroforestry, Crop Rotation, Ecosystem, etc. Defines “Forest Gardening as “multi-layered crop farming” or low maintenance and sustainable method of food production based on woodland ecosystems, incorporating fruit and nut trees, shrubs, herbs, vines, and perennial vegetables that yield directly useful to humans and a system of agroforestry that creates a diverse, productive, healthy, ecologically-sound and sustainable system of land use.
Seeks to transform farmers into multi-crop agripreneurs and help them build productive farming communities and produce high-quality crops;Â Intends to maximize land use, utilize idle lands, and inspire the youth toward sustainable agriculture.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE AND FOOD since 2024-04-29

rows.author: K089;K102;K140;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A SYSTEM OF REDISTRIBUTING AND RECYCLING FOOD WASTE TO PROMOTE FOOD SECURITY
rows.abstract:
Seeks to reduce food waste by promoting a National Zero Food Waste Campaign that shall entail various efforts to spread its awareness and information.Â  Provides waste reduction strategies for food-related businesses, households, and local government units to assist in financing and redistributing edible food waste to food banks and recycling inedible food waste through waste management facilities.

Defines several terms like “edible food waste” which refers to food discarded in the retail and consumption stages, determined to be fit for consumption based on standards set by the National Nutrition Council.

Proposes to exempt from donor´s tax - food-related businesses that donate edible food to food banks, and shall be considered as an allowable deduction from their gross income.
Â
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOOD SECURITY since 2024-04-29

rows.author: K089;K102;K140;
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING HAZARD PAY TO PUBLIC PROSECUTORS EXPOSED TO HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS AND PERFORMING HAZARDOUS DUTIES RELATED TO ASSIGNED CASES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Seeks to grant a hazard pay of 20% of the basic monthly salary to prosecutors who are subject to conduct the inquest, preliminary investigation, and prosecution of complex and high-profile crimes concerning graft and corruption, dangerous drugs (narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances), firearms and ammunition, money laundering, terrorism, arms smuggling, human trafficking, and other crimes against national security and public order.

Proposes that prosecutors exposed to hazardous situations, including an assignment in strife-torn or embattled areas, distressed or isolated situations, disease-infested areas - and areas declared under a state of calamity or emergency, will also be eligible for compensation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2024-04-29

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING GOVERNMENT AGENCIES AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS TO ALLOCATE AT LEAST 25% OF THEIR BUDGET FOR FURNITURE AND FIXTURES FOR PRODUCTS MADE OF ENGINEERED BAMBOO AND OTHER BAMBOO-BASED COMMODITIES
rows.title_short: Bamboo Products Procurement Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to recognize bamboo as a sustainable alternative to conventional materials, such as wood and steel.
Directs all agencies, departments, bureaus, offices and instrumentalities of the national government, as well as local government units (LGUs) to allocate a minimum of twenty-five percent (25%) of their annual furniture and fixtures budget for the procurement of engineered bamboo and bamboo-based products.
Mandates the Philippine Bamboo Industry Development Council to implement programs, conduct annual fairs or exhibits, develop a plan and program to increase the production of bamboo, identify government lands that may be planted with bamboo, work with SUCs with academic programs on forestry and agriculture to develop courses on the propagation of bamboo, and monitor the compliance of government agencies and LGUs.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2024-05-21, transmitted to the Senate on 2024-05-22 and received by the Senate on 2024-05-22

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE CAREER PROGRESSION SYSTEM FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Career Progression System For Public School Teachers Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to institutionalize the Career Progression System for public school teachers to promote professional development and career advancement among public school teachers.
Mandates the Civil Service Commission, Department of Education and Professional Regulation Commission to harmonize the qualification standards for teaching positions in all levels of the public school system.
Authorizes the Department of Budget and Management to create new teaching position titles of Teacher IV, Teacher V, Teacher VI, Teacher VII, and Master Teacher V, and include the same in the Index of Occupational Services, Occupational Groups, and Salary Grades.
Allows all incumbent Head Teachers to retain their positions and career progression line under the Current Career Progression, or otherwise apply for reclassification or retitling of their current position to the appropriate position under the Expanded Career Progression.
Prohibits the demotion in rank and/or diminution of salary, benefits and other privileges of incumbent employees granted under existing laws, decrees, orders of any contract, agreement or policy between employee and employer upon the implementation of this law.
Prescribes that teachers shall be promoted based on merit, fitness, and competence after a Comprehensive Performance Assessment.
rows.status: Republic Act RA12288 enacted on 2025-09-12

rows.author: K122;
rows.title_full:
AN ACT EXPANDING THE INVOLUNTARY SEPARATION BENEFIT, AMENDING FOR THE
PURPOSE SECTION 14-8 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11199, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS
THE "SOCIAL SECURITY ACT 0F 2018"
rows.abstract:
Seeks to expand the INVOLUNTARY UNEMPLOYMENT INSURANCE SEPARATION BENEFITS from fifty percent (50%) to SEVENTY-FIVE PERCENT (75%) of the qualified member´s Average Monthly Salary Credit (AMSC).

Aims to benefit workers in the private sector who fall in the lower echelons of the economic ladder and those with peculiar circumstances, including OFWs, solo parents, kasambahay, and similar covered groups.

rows.author: J093;K136;
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7638, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY ACT OF 1992
rows.abstract:
Proposes that no DIRECTOR, . . . CONSULTANT, OR ANY OTHER OFFICER of any private company or enterprise primarily engaged in the energy industry shall be eligible for appointment as Secretary within two years from his retirement. . .

Provides additional qualifications for appointment as Secretaries of the DOE - a person WITH AT LEAST TWO (2) YEARS OF ACTUAL WORK EXPERIENCE IN THE ENERGY SECTOR, AND WITH AT LEAST FIVE (5) YEARS OF ACTUAL AND DISTINGUISHED EXPERIENCE in any of the fields provided in the Act, including COMMERCE OR FINANCE . . .

Lays down a prohibition on the candidates and their relatives within the third civil degree of consanguinity or affinity from holding any interest in energy-related companies during their term; Seeks to impose a two-year period during which former DOE appointees are barred from accepting positions and engagements with energy industry players after termination of their service in the government.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2024-05-07

rows.author: K070;F008;K058;J015;G090;F076;K006;I054;K062;F062;K039;
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING AND INSTITUTIONALIZING ROLL-OVER DATA ALLOCATION SCHEME AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR NONCOMPLIANCE THEREWITH
rows.title_short: Roll - Over Internet Act
rows.abstract: Requires all Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to implement a Roll-Over Data Allocation Scheme for their subscribers as follows: a.) For postpaid subscribers or users: The rolled-over data allocation shall be prioritized to be consumed in the preceding month provided that the unused data every month shall be rolled-over and accumulated up until the last month and that all unused data allocation for a year may be used and converted as rebates; b.) For prepaid subscribers or users and postpaid subscribers who avail of internet data package promo offers: 1.) Unused data allocation shall be rolled-over provided that the subscriber or user renews the subscription right after the lapse of the offer duration: 2.) The unused data allocation of subscribers or users who fail to renew subscription shall be reduced by twenty percent (20%) everyday until the subscription is renewed; and 3.)  If the subscription is not renewed after five (5) days, all unused data allocation shall be considered consumed.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2024-07-30, transmitted to the Senate on 2024-07-30 and received by the Senate on 2024-07-30
